name: Build vs. Buy
title: Build vs. Buy Calculator
desc: Build vs. Buy calculator checks whether it pays off to build your own software tool rather than to buy it.

m.h: Cost per year
Additional costs of an employee.
How many days per time period will one employee spend on product maintenance?

c: annual_savings <= 0
Buy the tool as an external service — it will never pay off to build it!
years_to_profit <= 3
Building the tool will pay off in {{years_to_profit.formattedValue}} years — it is a good idea to build it!
years_to_profit <= 5 and years_to_profit > 3
Building the tool will pay off in {{years_to_profit.formattedValue}} years — there is a small chance of saving some money in the long run.
years_to_profit > 5
You should buy the tool as an external service — it will (most probably) never pay off to build it!

c: This burndown chart calculator will help you to track your sprint progress.
dayCount > 1

dayCount == 1
Since the sprint started {{dayCount.value}} day has passed. The team has burnt down {{spBurnt.value}} story points, with {{sp_difference.value}} story points remaining.

sprint_duration - dayCount == 0
​ ​ You have completed your sprint! Now look at your results:
sprint_duration - dayCount > 0
​ ​ The burndown speed required to complete all the tasks before the sprint ends is {{sp_speed_req_final.value}} story points / day. ⏱️
sprint_duration - dayCount == 0 and total_sp < spBurnt
​ ​ Well done, your team has done {{sp_excess.value}} story points over the target! ✨
sprint_duration - dayCount == 0 and total_sp == spBurnt

sprint_duration - dayCount == 0 and total_sp > spBurnt
​ ​ Oh no, your team has run out of time. ⌛ You should reflect this at your Sprint Retrospective and better plan your team's sprint next time.

name: Business loan
title: Business Loan Calculator
desc: Our business loan calculator helps you quickly estimate monthly payments and total loan costs, aiding in sound financial planning and understanding of your borrowing decisions.

m.h: While the nominal interest rate (or simply, the quoted rate) discloses only the interest on your loan amount, the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) reflects the real borrowing cost as it incorporates additional fees linked to the loan as well.
opts: I do not know either rate

m.h: Annual nominal interest rate or quoted rate.

Note that generally APR accounts for most fees, but there still might be other fees not included in the APR. For the list of typical charges, please refer to the text, and always check with your lender for accurate information.

c: The APR must be higher than the nominal interest rate. Please change the specifications.

m.h: Generally, banks in the U.S. apply interest calculation on a monthly bases. Still, it is always a good idea to confirm it with the lender as it may differ.
This is the full amount of the loan applied for. Note that the actual amount received may differ if any fee is financed by part of your loan.
This is the amount of money (or installment) that need to be paid by the agreed due date.
The length of time over which you are obliged to pay off your loan.
The regularity of the due payments.
Paid in advance before the beginning of the loan term – no interest is calculated on this fee but it is still included in the APR.
Rolled into the loan, and paid with the periodic installments–usually, banks calculate interest on this fee and include it in the APR.

You can include fees that are missed out from the quoted APR here. For the list of such possible charges, please refer to the text. It is always advisable to check with your lender on what fees they have based the APR. Note that charges included here are considered as prepaid fees.
It is also called the administration fee, underwriting fee, or processing fee. Note that it is given as a percentage of the whole loan amount and that APR usually includes this fee.
Mostly it is deducted from the loan amount and paid at the beginning of the loan term.

c: You receive a {{LoanReceived.monetaryValue}} loan after deducting the origination fee of {{fee_amount.monetaryValue}}.

name: Business valuation

desc: The business valuation calculator is here to help you discover the true worth of a company with ease and precision.

m.h: Choose a method to perform business valuation.
Enter the projected annual cash flow. This is the net amount of cash and cash equivalents being transferred into and out of the business.
Enter the total value of all business assets like cash, inventory, property, equipment, etc.
Enter total liabilities, including loans, accounts payable, and other debts.
Input all company-issued shares currently held by investors.
Price per one stock at the time of business valuation.
Specify the number of years you expect to forecast the cash flows. Typically, this is a 5 to 10-year period.
Input the yearly discount rate, which reflects the risk of the cash flows. Often, this is the weighted average cost of capital (WACC).

m.l: Earnings before interest, tax and amortization  (EBITA)

m.h: Provide an industry-specific multiple to calculate the terminal value. It can range from under 7 to over 20, depending on the industry. Here you can choose the industry, or "Custom" option to input custom value.

choose_multiple == 2

name: California tax
title: California Tax Calculator
desc: The California tax calculator helps you estimate how much tax you will pay for 2022.

m.h: Set here the period in which you want to see your take-home pay.
State here only the number of additional dependents — don't include yourself or your spouse.

Set here the total of itemized deductions other than retirement contribution relevant to the federal income tax. If you don't set a deduction or it is less than the standard deduction, the standard deduction will be considered.
Set here the assessed value of your property reduced by the applied exemption. In general, taxpayers can claim a $7,000 exemption on their owner-occupied homes.
The value reflects the average effective property tax rate levied in the selected county. You can update the tax rate if necessary.

Omni Example 1: Rental property — A rental property is worth $250,000 and generates $30,000 in annual gross rental income. Operating expenses represent 30% of the gross income, and a 5% vacancy rate during the year. What are the property’s annual net income and its cap rate?
property_value == 1200000 and gross_rental_income == 144000 and percent_operating_expenses == 0.35 and percent_vacancy_rate == 0.10

Omni Example 2: Commercial property — A commercial property is valued at $1,200,000 and generates $144,000 in annual gross income. Operating expenses account for 35% of the gross income, and the vacancy rate is 10%. What are the property’s annual net income and its cap rate?

m.h: Expressed as percentage of the gross income.

c: (property_value == 250000 and gross_rental_income == 30000 and percent_operating_expenses == 0.3 and percent_vacancy_rate == 0.05) or (property_value == 1200000 and gross_rental_income == 144000 and percent_operating_expenses == 0.35 and percent_vacancy_rate == 0.10)

How the result is calculated: Calculate the annual net income: Annual net income = Annual gross income × (1 − Operating expenses %) × (1 − Vacancy rate %) Determine the cap rate: Cap rate = Annual net income / Property value

name: Debt consolidation
title: Debt Consolidation Calculator
desc: Use the debt consolidation calculator to compare your current debts with a given consolidating loan.

m.h: Set the number of debts you would like to consolidate.
Monthly minimum payments means that you can increase your payments at any time. In contrast, when your payments are fixed, you cannot change the payment amount.
Here you can add any upfront financing fee that you need to pay before originating the loan.
Here you can set any financing fee that rolled into your loan.

c: _upfrontFeeFlag == 1
You need to pay an upfront fee of {{global.currencySymbol}}{{upfrontFeeValue.formattedValue}} for taking the consolidation loan.
_upfrontFeeFlag == 2
You need to pay an upfront fee of {{global.currencySymbol}}{{upfrontFeeValue.formattedValue}} to consolidate your debts.
_partialCoverageFlag == 1

As the consolidation loan only partially covers your debt, you need to finance {{global.currencySymbol}}{{partialCoverageValue.formattedValue}} in out of pocket expenses to consolidate your total debt.
_partialCoverageFeeFlag == 1
Besides, you need to pay an upfront fee of {{global.currencySymbol}}{{partialCoverageFeeValue.formattedValue}} for taking the consolidation loan.
_cashFlowFlag == 1
Since the consolidation loan exceeds your total debt amount, you would receive an upfront cash flow of {{global.currencySymbol}}{{cashFlowValue.formattedValue}} after making the transaction.
_cashFlowFeeFlag == 1
However, you need to pay an upfront fee of {{global.currencySymbol}}{{cashFlowFeeValue.formattedValue}} for taking the consolidation loan.
_aprComparisonFlag == 1

Since your consolidation loan's APR is higher than the estimated one for your total debts (APR of {{aprComparisonDebtAPR.formattedValue}}% vs. {{aprComparisonConAPR.formattedValue}}%), it's more expensive to consolidate your debts with the given loan from the perspective of cost of borrowing.
_aprComparisonFlag == 2

Since your consolidation loan's APR is lower than the estimated one for your total debts (APR of {{aprComparisonDebtAPR.formattedValue}}% vs. {{aprComparisonConAPR.formattedValue}}%), it's cheaper to consolidate your debts with the given loan from the perspective of cost of borrowing.
_aprComparisonFlag == 3

Since your total debt has about the same APR as the consolidation loan (both APRs are {{aprComparisonConAPR.formattedValue}}%), it doesn't make a significant financial difference to consolidate your debts with the given loan.
_pmtComparisonFlag == 1
Your monthly payments would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{pmtComparisonDiff.formattedValue}} more if you consolidated your debts.
_pmtComparisonFlag == 2
Your monthly payments would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{pmtComparisonDiff.formattedValue}} less if you consolidated your debts.
_pmtComparisonFlag == 3
Your monthly payments would be the same if you consolidated your debts.
_pmtComparisonFlag == 4
Your monthly payments would be set to {{global.currencySymbol}}{{pmtComparisonValue.formattedValue}} if you consolidated your debts.
_termInterestFlag == 1

Besides, you would have {{termInterestTermDiff.formattedValue}} more time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, but the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} more.
_termInterestFlag == 2

Besides, you would have {{termInterestTermDiff.formattedValue}} less time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, and the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} less.
_termInterestFlag == 3

Besides, you would have {{termInterestTermDiff.formattedValue}} more time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, but the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} less.
_termInterestFlag == 4

Besides, you would have {{termInterestTermDiff.formattedValue}} less time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, and the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} more.
_termInterestFlag == 5
Besides, you would have the same time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, but the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} less.
_termInterestFlag == 6
Besides, you would have the same time to repay your debt with the consolidation loan, but the charged interest would be {{global.currencySymbol}}{{termInterestIntDiff.formattedValue}} more.
PmtType != 1
If any of your debts require fixed payments, the APR is estimated by weighted average procedure.

name: Degree of operating leverage
title: Degree of Operating Leverage Calculator
desc: The degree of operating leverage calculator is an investing tool that provides you with a ratio that explains how much earnings can be influenced by a change in sales.

m.h: If you have the percentual change (period to period) of sales, put it here. Otherwise, add the specific period data in the section "Period to period specific data" above.
If you have the percentual change (period to period) of EBIT, put it here. Otherwise, add the specific period data in the section "Period to period specific data" above.

c: change_in_sales < 0 and change_in_EBIT < 0
Your company looks to be selling less and also producing less earnings. Better analyze its interest coverage ratio.
change_in_sales > 0 and change_in_EBIT < 0
Your company looks to be selling more, but suffering a reduction in its earnings. Better analyze its free cash flow.
change_in_sales < 0 and change_in_EBIT > 0
Your company looks to be selling less, but making more earnings. Better give a check to its inventory turnover ratio.
change_in_sales > 0 and change_in_EBIT > 0
Your company looks to be doing well. Sales and earnings are both growing. We recommend you to start checking how much you will profit from stocks.

name: Depreciation
title: Depreciation Calculator
desc: Depreciation calculator can find the value of an asset when using the straight-line method, declining balance method, and sum-of-years' digits method.

groups.title: Asset details
groups.desc: Choose the depreciation method to apply, enter the original cost, and the salvage value of the asset. Adjust the asset lifetime and end book point as needed.

m.h: The original value or purchasing price.
Also known as "Residual value". It represents the estimated amount of money an asset will be worth at the end of its lifetime.
The estimated number of years the asset is likely to remain in service.
The year at which you would like to compute the book value of the asset.
For this method, use a non-zero residual value.

name: Direct material price variance
title: Direct Material Price Variance Calculator
desc: Our direct material price variance calculator helps you determine the difference between the actual cost of direct materials and the standard cost.

m.h: Anticipated cost per unit based on budget or historical data.
Price actually paid for the materials.

c: direct_materials_price_variance > 0
As the direct materials price variance is positive, the direct materials price variance is unfavorable. This means that you are purchasing materials above their actual price.
direct_materials_price_variance < 0
As the direct materials price variance is negative, the direct materials price variance is favorable. This means that you are purchasing materials below their actual rate.
direct_materials_price_variance == 0
The direct materials price variance is zero. This means that you are purchasing materials at their actual rate.
